method.browser: isolated scripted Firefox 153 and Chromium sessions at DPR 1 with touch, mouse, and keyboard input against the frozen v0.2.2 trunk build
limitations: Persona satisfaction is a task-completion proxy, not measured user sentiment.
No real phone, tablet, on-screen keyboard, VoiceOver, TalkBack, or other screen reader participated.
The standard browser accessibility tree does not enumerate internal egui canvas controls; app-spoken keyboard feedback is an alternative, not equivalent support.
Chromium at DPR 1 does not establish Safari/iOS or Chrome/Android parity.

personas.label: First-time calculator user on a phone

evidence: Gross 767, selected yield, and expected good dies remain distinct and readable at 320 through 412 CSS pixels without horizontal overflow; inner viewport, visual viewport, canvas, body, and document widths matched each case.
A vertical W3C touch gesture (160,375 to 160,120) starting on Active width scrolled the page, did not open the editor, and left exported width at exactly 10.0 mm.
NaN and 0.1 mm were rejected in place with explicit messages; 10.25 mm applied with Enter and exported exactly.
Negative Binomial with alpha 2.5 is visible and editable at narrow widths, displaying 92.43%, and exported yield matched the independent oracle exactly (0.924274043305782).
390x844 to 844x390 to 390x844 retained exact dimensions without overflow and restored the original portrait pixels exactly; map, legends, and footer remained reachable.
The compact Report modal fit at 320 pixels; six Tabs wrapped to Close, Escape closed, Enter reopened, and the JSON export path remained keyboard-operable.

personas.label: Domain expert on a touch tablet

evidence: 768 and 820 use the intended single column; 1024, 1180, and 1440 use two complete columns without right-edge clipping.
A tap opens the numeric editor, while a swipe beginning on the same field scrolls without modifying diameter, dimensions, or D0; 1024 non-touch desktop keeps inline editing.
All five disclosure rows are full-row 44-point clickable targets, including their right-hand whitespace.
Alpha 2.5 gives exact yield 0.924274043305782 and expectation 708.9181912155348, matching an independent formula oracle; interface, export, and oracle agree.
Map, metadata, full A4 report, and JSON model metadata remain complete; the exported JSON reports calculator package version 0.2.2.

personas.label: Mouse user entering precise desktop values

evidence: 1024x768 uses two columns without clipping and retains inline DragValue editing when no touch capability is present, instead of opening the touch editor.
Changing Active width applies normally and changes Gross; the applied value is exported exactly.
NaN, infinity, and alphabetic text leave the prior value intact with an accurate invalid-entry message.
Probe columns rejects a non-whole number as not a finite whole number and preserves the prior value 4.

personas.label: Keyboard user on a constrained viewport

evidence: Report initially focuses Close, confines forward and reverse Tab to six modal actions, blocks background scrolling, and closes with Escape or backdrop activation.
After closing, focus returns to Report and Enter reopens the same modal; PageDown leaves the modal and background unchanged.
Enter applies a valid value directly from the focused touch-safe numeric editor.
Ctrl+Alt+S toggles app-spoken feedback from the canvas, and the visible footer control exposes the same state.
The canvas has an application role, accessible name, keyboard instructions, and an always-visible spoken-feedback control inside the app.
Visual keyboard navigation, editing, disclosure, model selection, and report export paths complete without a pointer.
A speechSynthesis interception receives the enabled-state announcement and subsequent focused-widget output.
eframe 0.36 Web does not forward its internal AccessKit tree to browser accessibility APIs, so standard screen readers cannot enumerate every canvas control.

An independent rectangle-grid oracle over the 300 mm / 3 mm-exclusion geometry reproduces gross 767, partial boundary 124, and edge-band 40 exactly; an independent Murphy triangular oracle reproduces yield 0.92360878014683934 and expectation 708.4079343726257.
For alpha 2.5 and exposure 0.08, the independent formula (1+0.08/2.5)^-2.5 reproduces yield 0.924274043305782 and expectation 708.9181912155348 exactly.

The native release report and the browser (WASM) export are byte-identical: sha256 fe01f45174017be68988fb986fe99f1076534a880653601f5fb2b9e8aff9e4cc for schema_version, calculation_metadata, normalized_inputs, results, probe_summary, and map_semantics; regenerating from current source reproduces the same bytes.

trunk build --release --public-url ./ from the current tree reproduces the frozen WASM artifact byte-for-byte: die-yield-gui-de88086fb34e83c6_bg.wasm sha256 681520e525c46d27068f2cea30169d1448644efee2b5a5cb9c320f5adee0e8c9.
Phone and tablet touch swipes starting over numeric fields scroll the page without changing the model or opening an editor.
NaN, infinity, alphabetic text, out-of-range values, and fractional integer fields are rejected without modifying the prior valid result.
Every tested phone and tablet has canvas, body, and document dimensions equal to its CSS viewport and no horizontal overflow.
Keyboard focus and scroll input remain inside Report until explicit close, after which focus returns to the invoking action.

findings.summary: A touch swipe beginning on a numeric field changed the value instead of scrolling
evidence: Confirmed resolved on the frozen v0.2.2 build: phone and tablet swipes over numeric fields scroll without changing the value or opening the editor.

findings.summary: Desktop NaN input silently changed a dimension while claiming it was rejected
evidence: Confirmed resolved on the frozen build: finite field-aware parsers reject NaN, infinity, alphabetic text, and fractional probe counts without changing the model.

findings.summary: Standard Web accessibility APIs do not enumerate internal egui canvas controls
evidence: The accessible canvas entry point, complete keyboard path, and optional app-spoken output reduce the gap but are not equivalent to a semantic DOM or Web AccessKit adapter.

findings.summary: Scenario comparison has no retained baseline or explicit delta
evidence: Deterministic JSON supports manual comparison, but the application still does not retain two named scenarios side by side.
